newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts fight back to end flat,short stg trounced.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts fight back to end flat,short stg trounced.

text.p: UK gilts fought back to end Wednesday unchanged after plummeting in morning trade following the release of very strong employment and retail sales data.
But short sterling failed to make back its losses and every listed contract ended the day lower.
Back dated contracts, from June 1997 to March 1998, suffered the biggest losses.
"The big fear is that the market doesn't get the rate rise it think the economy now needs, so even bigger rate rises will come later after the election," said a trader at a UK bank.
March short sterling settled at 93.28, down 0.14 on the day.
June, September and December all ended down 15 basis points lower. March gilt futures settled at 108-22, unchanged.
"The thin trading in gilts meant the momentum didn't build for a really big fall," said Mark Henry, financial analyst at GNI. "But the figures were really horrible for both gilts and short sterling."

Unemployment fell by 95,800 in November, the biggest monthly fall since records began, bringing the jobless total below the psychologically important two million level for the first time since early 1991. Other data showd retail sales rose by 0.7 percent in November.

Henry said market sentiment was damaged further by comments from Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke that inflationary pressures remain quite reasonable, and by employment secretary Gillian Shephard that the big drop in the jobless total was unlikely to be repeated.
"It sounded like they were playing it down."
Clarke and Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George meet on January 15 to discuss monetary policy.
November M4 data due at 0930 GMT on Thursday are unlikely to give the market much comfort.
The Reuter consensus forecast suggests a 0.8 percent monthly rise which would allow the year-on-year growth rate to ease to 10.1 percent from 10.3 percent in October.
The yield spread between gilts and Bunds widened to 193 basis points from 191 on Wednesday despite gilts' late comeback.
